title: Umbria's Petrol and Diesel Round-Trip Back to July Prices While Methane Keeps Climbing
dek: A four-month look at Umbria's daily fuel data shows Benzina and Gasolio erasing their autumn spike almost completely, while Metano prices have climbed nearly 50% since tracking began — outpacing the national increase by nine points.
executive_summary: On November 16, Umbria's self-service Benzina averaged €1.9756/L, essentially flat versus the previous day (€1.9765/L, -0.05%) and about €0.0029 above the national self-service average of €1.9727/L. Gasolio held almost perfectly steady at €2.2199/L (previous day €2.2201/L), running roughly 0.75% cheaper than Italy's €2.2366/L average. GPL, sold only at served pumps in this region, ticked up to €0.8557/L (+0.15% day-over-day) and now sits about 1.5% above the national served GPL price of €0.8433/L. Metano held flat at €2.1196/L, about 0.27% above the €2.1138/L national average. Umbria's 439 reporting stations out of 483 registered put its 90.9% reporting rate slightly ahead of Italy's 90.4%.

Zoom out to the weekly series tracked since July 21, though, and a sharper story emerges. Benzina and Gasolio both rode a clear spike through late summer into September — Benzina peaked near €2.1622/L in the week of September 21 (+9.8% from its July starting point) before sliding back to within half a percentage point of where it began; Gasolio followed the same arc, peaking near €2.3447/L before giving back more than 5% of that gain. Metano didn't follow the script: instead of reverting, it has climbed almost without pause, up roughly 50% in Umbria since late July — nearly nine percentage points faster than the 41% rise recorded nationally over the same stretch, making natural gas vehicle fuel this region's standout mover of the season.

fuel_sections.heading: Benzina: A Round Trip Back to Where It Started
paragraphs: Umbria's self-service Benzina closed at €1.9756/L on November 16, down a negligible 0.05% from €1.9765/L the day before, and running about €0.0029/L (0.15%) above the national self-service average of €1.9727/L — a gap that has narrowed to almost nothing after the region traded places with the national average several times over the past month.

The real movement happened earlier: Benzina rose from €1.9696/L in the week of July 20 to a peak of €2.1622/L in the week of September 21 — a 9.8% climb — before falling back 8.6% to €1.9770/L by the week of November 9, leaving the price just 0.4% above where the tracked series began nearly four months ago. Nationally the pattern was almost a mirror image: a 9.7% rise to a €2.1669/L peak in the same September week, followed by an 8.9% retreat to €1.9744/L — meaning Italy's national average actually finished very slightly (0.06%) below its starting point, while Umbria finished marginally above it.

fuel_sections.heading: Gasolio: Diesel's Steeper Climb, Shallower Retreat
paragraphs: Gasolio in Umbria priced at €2.2199/L on November 16, flat versus €2.2201/L the previous day, and running about €0.0167/L (0.75%) below the national self-service average of €2.2366/L — Umbria has consistently undercut the national diesel price through most of the autumn.

Over the tracked weeks, Umbria's Gasolio bottomed out at €2.0933/L in the weeks of August 3 and August 10, then climbed 12.0% to a €2.3447/L peak in the week of September 21, before easing back 5.3% to €2.2203/L by early November. That leaves the region's diesel price 3.3% above its late-July starting point of €2.1493/L — a slightly bigger net gain than the 2.9% increase recorded nationally over the same span, even though Umbria's trough-to-peak swing of 12.0% was marginally smaller than Italy's 12.3%.

fuel_sections.heading: GPL: The Fuel With No Self-Service Price in Umbria
paragraphs: Umbria's GPL is sold exclusively at served pumps in this dataset — not a single station in the region reports a self-service LPG price, which is why GPL is the only fuel missing from Umbria's weekly self-service averages. At the served pump, GPL reached €0.8557/L on November 16 (+0.15% day-over-day) and now sits about 1.5% above the national served average of €0.8433/L.

Measured on daily served prices since tracking began, Umbria's GPL has risen 10.2% — from €0.7763/L on July 21 to today's €0.8557/L — a steeper climb than the 9.0% increase in the national self-service GPL benchmark over the same period (€0.7592/L to €0.8277/L). The comparison isn't perfectly apples-to-apples given the different service tiers, but the direction is unambiguous: LPG has gotten more expensive faster in Umbria than the national trend suggests, on top of a market structure where every litre is pumped by an attendant.

fuel_sections.heading: Metano: The Fuel That Never Looked Back
paragraphs: Metano held at €2.1196/L in Umbria on November 16, unchanged from the day before, and running about €0.0058/L (0.27%) above the €2.1138/L national average — a small premium on a fuel that has moved more than any other this year.

Unlike Benzina and Gasolio, Metano never reverted: it climbed from €1.4135/L in the week of July 20 to €2.1196/L in the week of November 9, a 50.0% increase with essentially no pullback along the way. Nationally, the same fuel rose 40.9% over the identical span (€1.4999/L to €2.1132/L) — meaning Umbria's natural gas price has outpaced the national trend by close to nine percentage points, making Metano both the most volatile and the most one-directional fuel in this region's four-month history.

network_section.heading: A Network That Mostly Keeps Reporting
paragraphs: Umbria's registered station count has edged up only slightly since tracking began — from 481 stations on July 21 to 483 today, briefly touching 484 in early November. Of today's 483 registered stations, 439 reported a price on November 16, a 90.9% reporting rate that has stayed remarkably stable across the tracked period, generally holding between 437 and 439 stations reporting on any given day.

That 90.9% regional reporting rate runs slightly ahead of Italy's national figure of 90.4% (21,666 of 23,960 registered stations reporting on the same day), suggesting Umbria's relatively small, stable network reports with marginally more consistency than the national average — likely a function of having fewer stations to coordinate than larger regions.

methodology_section.heading: How This Report Gets Made
paragraphs: Everything above — the daily price pull from MIMIT's registries, the region-of-the-day rotation, the weekly trend calculations, and the prose you just read — is produced automatically every day by an unattended pipeline built with Claude Code, Anthropic's command-line coding agent. No analyst manually re-runs a spreadsheet formula or retypes a regional summary; the pipeline pulls the day's data, computes the real week-over-week and region-vs-national comparisons, and writes the report from those numbers each morning.

That stands in contrast to the way this kind of regional fuel-price reporting has traditionally been done — a manually maintained Excel sheet, updated by hand when someone remembers to, with charts that go stale the moment nobody has time to refresh them. The whole point of this project is to show that an AI coding agent can own the entire loop, from ingesting a public CSV feed to publishing an interactive dashboard and a written report, without a human touching the numbers in between.

closing.heading: Explore Beyond Umbria
paragraphs: The live Fuel Dashboard opens by default on Agip Eni's brand-level view, but that's just the starting point — use the scope picker to switch to Region, Province, Municipality, or another Operator/Brand and dig into whichever slice of Italy's fuel market you're actually curious about.

pull_quote: Metano has climbed 50% in Umbria since July — nine points faster than the national average, with no pullback in sight.
caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight: Umbria.

The headline isn't petrol or diesel — both have basically round-tripped back to where they started in July after a late-summer spike. It's Metano (natural gas) that stands out: prices in Umbria are up roughly 50% since tracking began in July, outpacing Italy's national 41% rise over the same period. Benzina sits at €1.98/L, Gasolio at €2.22/L, GPL at €0.86/L (served) and Metano at €2.12/L today, with Umbria's 439 reporting stations keeping a 90.9% reporting rate — just ahead of the national 90.4%.

This entire report — the data pull, the region rotation, the weekly trend analysis, even this write-up — is generated automatically every day by Fuel Dashboard, a self-updating pipeline I built with Claude Code instead of maintaining a manual Excel sheet. No one re-types numbers or redraws charts; the agent pulls the day's MIMIT data, computes the real week-over-week comparisons, and writes the regional report from scratch, every single day. It's a small example of what's possible when you hand an AI coding agent the whole loop — ingestion, analysis, and publishing — rather than just asking it to write a script.

Check out the live interactive dashboard at https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/ — switch the scope picker to Region, Province, Municipality, or a specific Operator/Brand to explore any slice of Italy's fuel market yourself.
